name: Gray + Otsu (baseline)
why: Simplest possible baseline: eggs are usually brighter than the background.
changes: grayscale, global Otsu, keep every bright pixel
decision_reason: Reference point: IoU 0.363; keeps every bright pixel, |count err| 1.47.

name: Gray + Otsu + morphology + largest blob
why: T01 keeps every bright pixel (cloth, walls, highlights); most images have one egg.
changes: open r=2, close r=4, keep largest component
decision_reason: IoU 0.363 -> 0.370 and |count err| 1.47 -> 0.47; 'largest blob' often picks wall/cloth instead of egg.

name: HSV white (low S, high V)
why: Egg is white: low saturation and bright; gray alone also picks up bright coloured areas.
changes: S <= 60 and V >= 70th percentile; open 2, close 4, largest
decision_reason: IoU 0.370 -> 0.429: a whiteness prior beats raw brightness.

name: Lab white cue + Otsu
why: Lab separates lightness from chroma more cleanly than HSV, and the cue is continuous so Otsu adapts per image.
changes: score = norm(L) * (1 - chroma/40); Otsu; open 2, close 4, largest
decision_reason: Mean IoU 0.416 (vs 0.429) but BF1 0.259 -> 0.298 and instance F1 up; a continuous 0-1 cue is needed to fuse more cues.

name: T04 + egg-shape component selection
why: T02-T04 worst cases: 'largest bright blob' is often the wall, a label or white cloth, not the egg.
changes: select = blobs with solidity >= 0.85 and ellipse aspect <= 2.2, keep those >= 20% of the biggest
decision_reason: IoU 0.416 -> 0.439, instance F1 0.347 -> 0.405: shape beats size for choosing the egg.

name: T05 + border background model
why: White-on-white scenes (bag, tray, white box): egg and background are both white, so the white cue merges them. Border pixels are mostly background, so 'different from the border colours' separates them.
changes: k-means (k=4) on border-ring Lab pixels (L weight 0.5); cue = distance to nearest centre; score = geometric mean(white, bg)
decision_reason: IoU 0.439 -> 0.484, median 0.308 -> 0.536, |count err| 0.33 -> 0.16: fixes most white-on-white scenes.

name: T06 + smoothness cue
why: Textured backgrounds (ash, cloth, carpet, keyboard) have pale pixels that pass the white and bg cues; eggshell is smooth.
changes: cue = exp(-local std of L in 7x7 / 8); score = geometric mean(white, bg, smooth)
decision_reason: IoU 0.484 -> 0.427 and BF1 0.317 -> 0.047: texture is high exactly on the egg outline, so the mask shrinks.

name: T06 + multi-level threshold selection
why: T06 worst cases: at the single Otsu level the egg merges with cloth/bag/tray into one irregular blob, the shape filter rejects it and keeps a speck. At some other level the egg is a clean ellipse.
changes: 16 thresholds between the 20th and 99.5th score percentile; candidates need fill >= 0.75, solidity >= 0.85, aspect <= 2.2; quality = fill * solidity * (inside - ring contrast); greedy keep with overlap suppression, keep quality >= 0.6 * best
decision_reason: IoU 0.484 -> 0.492, precision 0.663 -> 0.779; recall drops (bright core only) but it gives clean seeds for GrabCut.

name: T08 + GrabCut refinement + hole fill
why: T08 has precision 0.78 but recall 0.52: it finds the right object but keeps only the bright core (shaded side of the egg falls below the chosen level). GrabCut grows it using colour models.
changes: GrabCut init: selected blobs = probable FG, eroded core = sure FG, beyond a 15% margin = sure BG; 5 iters; re-select egg-shaped blobs; fill holes per instance
decision_reason: IoU 0.492 -> 0.553, BF1 0.342 -> 0.471: GrabCut recovers the shaded side of the egg.

name: T09 + candidates from 5 maps (contrast rank)
why: T09 gives no prediction on 8 dev images (ash, foil, bag, tray): the combined score never isolates the egg. Cue maps show the egg separates in *some* map (L, white, bg) or as an edge-enclosed region.
changes: multilevel candidates from score, white, bg, L and Canny-enclosed regions; same contrast ranking
decision_reason: Mean IoU 0.553 -> 0.549 but median 0.618 -> 0.674 and recall 0.569 -> 0.642; bigger candidate pool needed for better ranking.

name: T10 with edge-support ranking
why: Contrast in a cue is weak exactly where cues fail; but the egg outline always sits on a strong luminance edge.
changes: quality = fill * solidity * fraction of outline pixels on gradients above the 80th percentile
decision_reason: IoU 0.549 -> 0.444: edge-only ranking prefers round background structures (tray cups, bowl rims).

name: T10 with contrast + edge ranking
why: Combine both kinds of evidence: contrast rejects background patches, edges reject cue noise.
changes: quality evidence = mean(contrast, edge support)
decision_reason: IoU 0.500, below contrast-only T10.

name: T10 with ring-contrast + size ranking
why: Candidate diagnostic on T10: best candidate in the pool averages IoU 0.68 but the top-ranked one 0.51 (best is ranked first on only 10% of images). Good candidates are larger (median 8% vs 0.9% of the image) and whiter / more unlike the border than the ring around them (AUC 0.89 / 0.80).
changes: quality = fill * solidity * (max(white_in - white_ring, 0) + max(bg_in - bg_ring, 0)) * area^0.25 (formula picked offline on dev candidates: top-1 IoU 0.51 -> 0.56)
decision_reason: IoU 0.549 -> 0.568, median 0.697, recall 0.723: ranking picks whole eggs instead of fragments.

name: T13 without GrabCut
why: T13 worst cases include leaks (IoU 0.2-0.36 with low precision) on cloth, bag, rice and food container: the right egg is chosen, then GrabCut floods into similar-coloured background. Ablation.
changes: grabcut off (candidate + hole fill only)
decision_reason: Ablation: IoU 0.568 -> 0.541 and BF1 0.510 -> 0.403 without GrabCut, so GrabCut stays; leaks come from wrong candidates, not GrabCut.

name: T13 with tighter GrabCut margin
why: Limit how far GrabCut may grow: sure-background starts closer to the candidate.
changes: gc_bg_margin 0.15 -> 0.05
decision_reason: IoU 0.568 -> 0.548: tighter margin cuts off real egg as well as leaks.

name: T13 with guarded per-egg GrabCut
why: Keep GrabCut's gain where it works (shaded side of the egg) and undo it where it leaks.
changes: GrabCut per selected egg; revert to the candidate if it grows > 1.6x, or solidity < 0.85, or aspect > 2.2
decision_reason: IoU 0.568 -> 0.573 but median 0.697 -> 0.659 and |count err| 0.23 -> 0.41; not worth the complexity.

name: T13 + mean-shift candidate maps
why: 14 dev images have no usable candidate at all (dusty eggs on ash, white-on-white bag/tray/rice). Mean-shift filtering flattens texture but keeps strong edges, so a dusty egg becomes one uniform blob.
changes: extra candidate maps: L, white and bg computed on a mean-shift filtered image (sp=12, sr=24)
decision_reason: IoU 0.568 -> 0.553 and 0.73 s/img; candidate oracle only 0.678 -> 0.695.

name: T13 + multi-radius opening of candidates
why: In the remaining misses the egg is a thick convex blob joined to background by a thin bridge at every threshold (egg base touching the white bag, the tray, the rice). A larger opening cuts the bridge.
changes: each threshold level opened with radius 1, 4 and 8 px (at 320 px work size)
decision_reason: Mean IoU 0.562 (flat) but candidate oracle 0.678 -> 0.755 with no image below 0.18; enables T19.

name: T18 + ranking with edge, centre and shape terms
why: T18 raised the candidate-pool oracle from 0.68 to 0.76 but top-1 stayed ~0.56: ranking is now the bottleneck. On T18 dev candidates, distance from centre (AUC 0.22, i.e. good ones are central), edge support (0.76) and shape add information to the ring contrast.
changes: quality = shape^2 * (white_d + bg_d) * area^0.25 * (0.5 + edge_support) * (1 - centre_distance) (offline top-1 on dev candidates 0.56 -> 0.60)

name: T19 + watershed split of touching eggs
why: Marble-counter images have 2-3 touching eggs; GrabCut can merge them into one blob (count error -1/-2).
changes: distance-transform watershed per blob; split only if 2+ peaks above 0.6 * max distance
decision_reason: IoU unchanged (0.593), |count err| 0.18 -> 0.25: splits single eggs with highlights more often than it separates touching eggs.

name: T19 + ellipse regularisation
why: Eggs are near-ellipses; replacing each mask by its fitted ellipse could fix ragged GrabCut edges and shadow bites.
changes: replace instance by fitted ellipse when mask fills >= 85% of it
decision_reason: IoU 0.593 -> 0.572, BF1 0.528 -> 0.364: SAM masks follow occluders (fingers, leaves, rods), an ellipse cannot.

name: T19, keep more eggs (rel quality 0.4)
why: Multi-egg images are under-counted more often than over-counted.
changes: ml_rel_quality 0.6 -> 0.4
decision_reason: IoU 0.593 -> 0.543, instance F1 0.571 -> 0.495: extra false eggs.

name: T19, keep fewer eggs (rel quality 0.8)
why: Opposite direction of T22, to bracket the parameter.
changes: ml_rel_quality 0.6 -> 0.8
decision_reason: IoU 0.593 -> 0.590, instance F1 up but |count err| 0.18 -> 0.30 (misses real second/third eggs); keep 0.6.

name: T19 + whiteness gate on candidates
why: T19 failures are mostly wrong picks (29 of the IoU<0.5 images have precision < 0.5): orange lid, blue print on the bag, foil. 99% of good dev candidates have mean white cue >= 0.54.
changes: drop candidates with mean white cue < 0.5 (offline top-1 0.601 -> 0.609)
decision_reason: IoU 0.593 -> 0.612, median 0.758, Dice 0.684, P 0.718, R 0.761, BF1 0.545, instance F1 0.613, |count err| 0.16; best on every metric.
